title: High-Accuracy Propagation-Assisted Local Decoding for Fast Transversal Clifford Circuits
authors: Mark Webber, Simanraj Sadana, Matthew A. Lane, Lucy Jade Robson, Anthony O'Rourke
abstract: We benchmark the Iterative Redecode Scheme (IRS) on fast transversal Clifford circuits, achieving high-accuracy correlated decoding using local memory-style detectors and decoders. On a deep random Clifford benchmark, IRS yields approximately $4\times$ lower logical failure rates than the ghost protocol at $d=11$ with matched buffers, and $15\times$ lower rates than logical observable matching (LOM). In three-block GHZ preparation, IRS achieves $2\times$ lower logical error rates than reliable logical Pauli-product decoding with matched initialisation, improving to $25\times$ at $d=19$ with $\lceil d/2\rceil$ full initialisation rounds. We place IRS, which builds on Wan et al.'s scheme, within a broader propagation-assisted local (PAL) framework, where local decoders exchange messages rather than decoding a global hypergraph. IRS alternates local minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) on memory-equivalent detector error models (DEMs) with Pauli-frame propagation and detector updates across transversal CNOT layers, seeking local error estimates consistent with the global detector record. Prior-informed DEMs account for probabilities of propagated errors missing from the memory-equivalent model, improving initial decoding and reducing logical error rates. Zero-weight physical Pauli mechanisms enable inference and propagation of initially indeterminate stabilizer outcomes. Error rates saturate after a few iterations even for deep, adversarial alternating-tCNOT circuits, allowing iteration caps with negligible loss of accuracy. We find syndrome-extraction buffers of order $\lfloor d/4\rfloor$ sufficient for distance-dependent error suppression in the demanding regimes studied. The approach extends to other local decoders and CSS codes; for repeated logical $S$ gates, IRS achieves approximately $4$ to $10\times$ lower logical error rates than LOM, depending on initialisation.
summary: This paper introduces the Iterative Redecode Scheme (IRS), a powerful decoding technique for fault-tolerant quantum computation using transversal Clifford circuits. IRS operates within a Propagation-Assisted Local (PAL) framework, iteratively refining error estimates by combining local matching with error propagation across circuit layers. It demonstrates superior performance over existing methods, making it a significant advancement for building reliable quantum computers.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving high-accuracy decoding for fault-tolerant quantum computation, specifically dealing with correlated error structures arising from error propagation across multiple logical blocks in transversal Clifford circuits.
main_result: The proposed Iterative Redecode Scheme (IRS) significantly lowers logical failure rates compared to established protocols like the ghost protocol and Logical Observable Matching (LOM) across deep random and structured benchmarks.
method: IRS implements a Propagation-Assisted Local (PAL) framework by iteratively alternating local minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) decoding with Pauli-frame propagation and detector updates across transversal CNOT layers.
model_or_system: The work focuses on fault-tolerant quantum computation using surface codes and general CSS codes, simulating circuits involving successive transversal CNOT (tCNOT) layers.
key_observables: Logical failure rates, detector records, and the consistency between local and global error estimates.
important_parameters: Code distance (d), number of syndrome-extraction buffer rounds ($\lfloor d/4floor$), and error probabilities ($p$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that local decoders can be coupled via message passing (PAL framework) and that the error process can be modeled by propagating Pauli errors across gate boundaries.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the logical error rate vs. code distance for IRS against the ghost protocol and LOM on a deep random Clifford benchmark. Other figures detail circuit schematics for GHZ preparation and repeated logical S gates.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the IRS as an extension of the PAL framework, detailing its iterative mechanism (MWPM $\leftrightarrow$ Propagation). It then benchmarks this scheme against state-of-the-art decoders on various deep circuits (random Clifford, GHZ, repeated S gates), concluding with discussions on the underlying error models and necessary buffer sizes.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation, the core concept of iterative refinement and propagating local constraints to solve a global, correlated problem shares conceptual parallels with advanced techniques in statistical physics and optimization.
